concept: List prints rows of devices or tracks on one plastic body, the way an appliance prints its programmes on the case, with a glyph or a printed index, a name, the state in words and at most one part to work at the end of the row.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material list with avatar circles, two line text and divider lines everywhere
default_to_avoid.why_not: Avatar circles and full width divider rules turn every row into a separate tile, so the rows read as a table of contacts instead of printing on one device body.

default_to_avoid.pattern: list of separate cards, one raised card per row
default_to_avoid.why_not: A shadow under every row makes each row look like a unit to open and multiplies the shadows that P6 keeps short and few.

references.source: Braun TG 60 tape recorder (Dieter Rams, 1965): the counter and functions printed in one column on the case, set apart by space, not rules
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): rows of keys and printing on one body, kept apart by an even gap

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: Every row starts its glyph, index and words on the same inset line of one body, and rows are set apart by an even gap instead of seams.

derivation.consequence: capped so large panels do not swell into pillows
derivation.form: The body takes corner.panel and a row's recess takes corner.inner, so the row nests in the body with inner equal to outer minus the inset.
A row that opens something is printing on the body; pressed, it sinks into a small recess with the inverse light, and it never rises on hover.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: A chosen row in a queue is marked by an ink index mark and medium weight; no row is ever filled with orange or any tint.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Every row is at least control.lg tall and the whole row is the target when it opens something, so a finger never aims at a word.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: A printed track index uses tabular figures in secondary ink, so the column of numbers stays straight from 1 to 99.

options.name: gaps on one body: rows printed on one plastic body, the pressed row a nested recess, an ink mark on the chosen row
seams on one body: rows edge to edge with a hairline seam between each pair
one small raised unit per row, stacked with gaps

variants.reason: A keeps one body and one shadow for the whole list and separates rows by space, which FORM's separator rule asks for first (gaps first); B draws a seam between every pair of rows inside one unit, which FORM forbids as hard rules between regions, and C gives every row its own shadow and makes each row look like a card to open, against P6 shadows are short and soft.

root.why: The list is one body of matte plastic with the unit shadow, so it paints its own surface wherever it is dropped.

item.why: Each item is one line of the list body, set apart from the next by an even gap instead of a seam.

row.why: The row lays its glyph, words and end part along the body's inset line with one gap between each of them.

action.why: A row that opens something is one link or button the full size of the row, at least 52px tall for a finger.

selectable.why: A queue list is one listbox in the tab order, and the arrow keys move the active row within it.

lead.why: The leading glyph sits in a fixed column at the start of the row, so every name starts on one line.

index.why: A printed track number uses tabular figures in the label size, so a column of numbers keeps its width.

text.why: The words take the free width of the row and wrap, so a long name never pushes the end part off the body.

primary.why: The name is the body size in regular weight with a line box tall enough for stacked Thai tone marks.

secondary.why: The state in words is secondary ink above 4.5:1 on the plastic, printed one size down under the name.

trail.why: The end of the row holds at most one part, such as a switch or a key, so a row never has two loud controls.

chevron.why: A printed chevron at the end tells that the row opens another page, flat ink with no shadow and no emboss.

mark.why: The chosen row carries a short ink index mark at its start edge, never an orange or tinted fill behind the words.

hover.why: Hover only darkens the printed chevron a step, because a row does not rise or change colour when a pointer comes near.

active.why: A pressed row sinks into a small recess with the inverse light at once, the way a part drops when it is pressed.

focus-visible.why: The focused row shows the same dark ring as every part in dial, drawn inside the row so the body does not cut it.

disabled.why: A disabled row fades to half and loses its pointer, so it reads as not taking a press right now.

aria-disabled=true.why: A disabled option in a queue fades to half and the keys and the pointer cannot choose it.

aria-selected=true.why: The chosen row is medium weight with its ink index mark lit, so the choice is shape and weight, not hue.

data-active=true.why: The row the arrow keys point to carries the focus ring while the list has focus, so the keyboard position is always visible.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the body keeps a real border and the ring and the index mark use the system highlight colour.
